rawFindings.title: Incorrect Content-Range header end byte in range request handling
rawFindings.explanation: The code sets the Content-Range header as 'bytes start-end/length' but actually slices responseData with slice(start, end + 1). Since slice is exclusive of the end index, the Content-Range end byte should be 'end' - 1 to reflect the actual byte range served. The current code will cause clients to think one more byte is sent than actually is, leading to protocol inconsistencies or client errors.
rawFindings.suggestion: Change the Content-Range header end byte to 'end' instead of 'end'. For example, set it as 'bytes ' + start + '-' + (end) + '/' + responseData.length, but ensure the slicing and header match. Alternatively, correct the slicing or header so that the number of bytes matches.
rawFindings.failureAfterChange: A request for a byte range 'bytes=3-8' on a 9-byte resource returns a Content-Range header of 'bytes 3-9/9' but response body with bytes 3 to 8 (6 bytes). Clients expecting 7 bytes (3 to 9) will detect truncated data or other issues.
